messages:
Danielle K: quick security check — we want to enable a temporary capture of full request+response bodies for a Dedicated customer in staging to debug a production-only error. bodies include customer emails and sometimes user-supplied tokens. asking: is there an approved minimal-scope approach that avoids storing PII/tokens but keeps enough context for debug? :thinking:

Ash Patel: short answer: tokens must never be stored in plaintext. emails are PII — either redact or pseudonymize. also need IAM gating + audit log for whoever fetches the traces.

Danielle K: thanks. proposal: capture 24h, store in S3 bucket with SSE-KMS, access via presigned url expiring in 48h. redact tokens fully (`<REDACTED_TOKEN>`) and pseudonymize emails as `email_hash:<first4>...` using HMAC-SHA256 with a team key. sample at 1% overall, but keep full captures for the affected customer's requests only. Thoughts?

Ash Patel: okay but a few points:
- HMAC key must be stored in KMS, not checked into repo.
- For tokens, prefer replacing with a deterministic placeholder plus length info (e.g., `<REDACTED_TOKEN_len=43>`) so devs know size without seeing contents.
- For customer-scoped full captures we need explicit approval from Customer Success + Legal if data includes EU users.

Mike R: ops note: we can flip a feature flag `ENABLE_STAGING_BODY_CAPTURE` per-customer. simple config snippet:```yaml
capture:
  enabled: true
  scope: customer:acme-corp
  sample_rate: 0.01
  redact_headers: ["authorization", "x-api-key"]
  redact_tokens: true
```
I'll also add an IAM role `staging-trace-reader` that requires approval to assume.

Danielle K: perfect. is the HMAC approach acceptable for debugging who sent which email without exposing actual address? Eve, any legal concerns for EU customers? @Eve (Legal)

Eve (Legal): HMAC/pseudonymization is fine as long as the HMAC key is rotated and access is limited. For EU data, we need documented justification (debugging incident) and retention capped — suggest 7 days unless CS requests extension. Also log who requested access.

Ash Patel: add: enforce `redact_tokens = true` at the middleware level so no dev path can accidentally opt-out. Also strip prompt-level traces that may contain tokens or secrets.

Danielle K: got it. one more ask — are we allowed to include a tiny excerpt of the response (first 200 chars) in plaintext even if it contains an email? proposal: keep first 20 chars, then pseudonymize any email pattern.

Ash Patel: ok to include excerpt if you run an automated scrub for email patterns and replace with `email_hash:xxx`. no manual eyeballing of raw emails.

security-bot: Incident access policy reminder: Any request for `staging-trace-reader` must include ticket link and approval from CS + Legal.

Mike R: I'll push the flag + middleware changes to a feature branch and add a retention lifecycle rule on the S3 path `s3://redwood-staging-traces/acme-corp/` to expire objects after 7 days. Presigned URLs will be 48h max.

Danielle K: thanks everyone — I'll create the ticket and tag CS + Legal for approval. tagging @Ash for final sign-off on the HMAC approach. :thumbsup:

Ash Patel: sign-off from security: HMAC pseudonymize emails, redact tokens with length placeholder, KMS keys + IAM gating, 7-day retention for EU by default, 48h presigned links, manual extension only with CS+Legal written approval. :white_check_mark:

Danielle K: awesome, closing this thread — will attach ticket number when created.
